name: SmartComply Academy Certificates
description: Certificate management and public verification for SmartComply Academy, a training and certification platform for cybersecurity professionals. Admins search, filter and export every certificate issued; anyone can check a certificate by its ID and see exactly what they should, and nothing more.
role: Senior software engineer: built verification, status rules and the admin list
contributions: Built the public verification endpoint and the Verify page: lookup by certificate ID only, every lookup recorded
Put the certificate status rules (active, suspended, withdrawn, expired) in one module, with an event on expiry
Added search, date ranges and a pathway filter to the admin list, plus row actions
Built a formula-safe CSV export of everything that matches
Stacked my work on two colleagues' open pull requests and wrote the merge order, so three PRs merged without conflicts
results: 353 of 353 backend tests pass with all four PRs combined

body.heading: The problem
paragraphs: An accreditation sprint needed three things at once: certificate status rules enforced in one place, a public verification page that reveals only what it should, and an admin list that can be searched, filtered and exported. Four engineers were changing the same files.

body.heading: What I built
paragraphs: Verification answers by certificate ID alone and shows the holder, the certification and its status; every lookup is recorded. Status (active, suspended, withdrawn or expired) is decided in one module, with an event when a certificate expires. The admin list gained search across holder, certification and scheme, date ranges, a pathway filter loaded from the server, row actions, and a CSV export in which any cell that would run as a spreadsheet formula is neutralised.

body.heading: Keeping four people's merges clean
paragraphs: Instead of racing to merge first, I rebased my backend work onto a colleague's open pull request and wrote the merge order (theirs, then mine), and stacked the front end the same way on another colleague's. The reviewer merged three pull requests without a conflict, and nobody's work was undone.
